title: WPMS/2833/2024 of RENU TOMAR Vs DISTRICT ELECTION OFFICER

paras.text:
2025:UHC:8840
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Misc. Single No.2833 of 2024
07 October, 2025
Renu Tomar --Petitioner
Versus
District Election Officer and Ors. --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Rajendra Singh Azad, learned counsel for the
petitioner, appeared through video conferencing.
Mr. Prem Prakash Bhatt, learned counsel holding
brief of Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, learned counsel for the
respondent Nos.1, 3, 5, 6 and 7.
Mr. Anil Dabral, learned Additional C.S.C. with Mr.
Sudhir Nailwal, learned Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand/respondent Nos.2 and 4.
None appeared for respondnet Nos.8 and 11 despite
service.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
 Counter affidavit filed by the State is taken
on record. Miscellaneous Application (IA/4/2025)
made therefor, is allowed.
2. By means of the present writ petition,
petitioner has put to challenge the order dated
09.09.2024 passed by learned Prescribed
Authority/Assistant Collector-1st Class/Sub
Divisional Magistrate, Roorkee, District Haridwar
(hereinafter referred as 'Prescribed Authority') in
Election Petition No.03 of 2022-23 Smt. Renu Tomar
Vs. Chief Election Officer and Others, whereby, the
application dated 16.03.2024 moved by the petitioner
under Order 16 Rule 10 read with Section 151 of CPC
has been rejected.
1

2025:UHC:8840
3. Petitioner contested the election of Gram
Sabha, Gram Panchayat Sakoti unsuccessfully. She
filed an election petition before the learned
Prescribed Authority under Section 131H of the
Uttarakhand Panchayati Raj Act, 2016, against the
respondents including returned candidate-Km.
Vidushi Panwar (respondent No.8). During the
course of election petitioner, an application dated
16.03.2024 was moved by the petitioner, which is
annexed as annexure No.7 to the writ petition,
calling upon the learned Prescribed Authority to
direct the respondent No.1-District Election
Officer/District Magistrate, Haridwar to produce
certain documents enumerated in the said
application, which according to the petitioner were
necessary for proper adjudication of the matter.
4. The said application moved by the
petitioner was rejected by the learned Prescribed
Authority vide impugned order dated 09.09.2024 on
the ground that the documents sought by the
petitioner were kept in the double lock and that can
only be opened by the order of the learned
Competent Court/District Judge.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for
the petitioner that since the election petition is being
contested before the learned Prescribed Authority
under Section 131H of the Uttarakhand Panchayati
Raj Act, 2016, therefore, in this case, the Competent
Authority is not the District Judge but the Prescribed
Authority itself and it is only after the order passed
by the learned Prescribed Authority, the documents
2

2025:UHC:8840
required by the petitioner can be produced by the
learned District Election Officer/District Magistrate,
Haridwar in the Election Tribunal i.e. Prescribed
Authority.
6. This argument advanced by the learned
counsel for the petitioner has also not been disputed
by the learned State Counsel, as in the case in hand,
the Competent Authority is the Prescribed Authority,
where the election petition is pending.
7. In such view of the matter, the impugned
order dated 09.09.2024 is bereft of merit and
deserves to be set aside. Accordingly, the impugned
order dated 09.09.2024 passed by learned Prescribed
Authority in Election Petition No.03 of 2022-23 Smt.
Renu Tomar Vs. Chief Election Officer and Others, is
hereby set aside. The Prescribed Authority shall pass
a fresh order on the application dated 16.03.2024
moved by the petitioner in accordance with law.
8. Accordingly, the present writ petition is
allowed.
9. Pending application(s), if any, stands
disposed of.
